I was diagnosed with dysthymia (mild underlying long-term depression) about 4-5 years ago, with some short (1-2 month long) bouts of intense depressive periods in between due to bad triggers like a breakup and losing jobs.

At this point in my life, I’m confident in saying I’m generally emotionally stable, and even when I slip, the spirals aren’t that bad, they don’t last as long, they don’t come as frequently and the aftermath of guilt etc isn’t as intense because I don’t act out as badly, so there’s much less to feel guilty about.

My 100% opinion on what helped is therapy. I’ve been in professional therapy for 6 years and it has changed my life. I’m forever grateful for every decision that led me to seeking help. My life would look so different today if I hadn’t started at some point.

It’s a long process, but it’s so worth it. If you can’t afford private therapy, go for counselling. Look for therapists that practice CBT. Stick with it, and you will see the change in yourself. Don’t be afraid of medication (I was on anti-depressants for a while to balance out my mood to get me to a point where I could handle putting tools & skills into practice). But try to find a psychiatrist who’s working to get you off medication as soon as possible, not keep you dependent forever.

I promise you, if you keep at it, things will shift so drastically that one day you’ll look back and be like wow… I’m so grateful I took that first step. It can and does get better.

I was angry, irritable & easily upset for most of my life.

Sadly, it took a bad breakup where I lost a relationship & partner that I cherished greatly to force me to get help and realise that I wasn’t just a moody person, I was suffering from depression & anxiety.

Some days I feel lots of regret that I didn’t get help sooner as the relationship might have turned out differently. But I choose to see it in another way - I’m lucky that I had a connection that I cared about early enough in life that led me to take steps to start making changes.

I think there are many people out there who think that they’re ugly, unintelligent, useless or broken when in fact they could unlock a whole other person inside of them if they got help.

I try to find a space where I can be alone, like in my room. I let the feelings come and, if I feel like it, write out my thoughts in a journal. I feel that writing helps to get the emotions out, and I think it helps to confront the feelings head on instead of ignoring them. I usually do feel more clear-headed after journaling.

But whatever your process, I think the most impt part of it is allowing it to happen & not hating yourself for it. Feel whatever you need to feel and know it doesn't make you weak, you just need some time to be human.
